label: TP
reason: User-controlled header value flows directly into response output via concatenation without effective neutralization. The chain of transformations (URL decoding, substring, Base64 round-trip, split) does not reliably sanitize arbitrary XSS payloads; specifically, splitting on space and truncating characters does not prevent script execution if the payload avoids those patterns or uses encoded entities. The sink writes the resulting string to response.getWriter(), enabling XSS.

evidence.note: user header value flows through transformations and is concatenated into response output without reliable neutralization
